name: Oxabolone cipionate

lead: Oxabolone cipionate is a long-acting injectable ester of oxabolone (4-hydroxy-19-nortestosterone), a nandrolone-type anabolic steroid, marketed in Europe as Steranabol Depo and Steranabol Ritardo. People who follow steroid history mention it for mass gain.

It is a prodrug of oxabolone, given by intramuscular injection, and carried the developmental code FI-5852. Very little has been published: sources do not describe its pharmacology or potency in detail, and no clinical or appearance studies were found.

paras: It was marketed as a depot injectable in Europe. Little else is documented about its use.
The only indexed medical report found is a 1995 dermatology paper on mucosal hyperpigmentation attributed to oxabolone. Little else is documented.

angle.text: Oxabolone cipionate is mentioned for mass gain as a nandrolone-type steroid that activates androgen receptors. It was once sold in Europe as Steranabol, and almost nothing about it has been published.

lead: Oxabolone cipionate (also spelled cypionate) is a synthetic injected anabolic-androgenic steroid of the 19-nortestosterone (nandrolone) group. It is the C17β cypionate ester and a prodrug of oxabolone, and it carried the developmental code FI-5852. It has been marketed in Europe under the brand names Steranabol Depo and Steranabol Ritardo. [1]

Published information is sparse. Wikipedia does not describe indications, pharmacokinetics or regulatory status, and the one indexed medical paper is a case report of mucosal hyperpigmentation attributed to oxabolone. [1][2]

paras: Oxabolone cipionate has the formula C26H38O4 and is a 3-cyclopentylpropanoate ester of 4-hydroxy-19-nortestosterone. Related compounds include clostebol, norclostebol, formestane and 4-hydroxytestosterone. [1]
A 1995 report in Acta Dermato-Venereologica described mucosal hyperpigmentation due to oxabolone. [2]
No studies found. The only indexed human report is a case report of mucosal hyperpigmentation with oxabolone. [2]
